title: Fit a palm-protector cone into a care manikin's contracted hand, its curled fingers held open and eased down onto it
instruction: Fit the padded palm cone into the curled hand of the plastic training-manikin arm on the pad: the cone lying across the palm under the fingers, its narrow end at the thumb, with all four fingertips resting on it. Do not force the fingers, keep the hand on the pad, and let go when it is in.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00, 1.4 million US jobs) and personal care aides fit hand devices to residents with contracted hands as part of daily care. The open textbook Nursing Assistant (9.4): "a cone that slides into the palm of the hand ... The cone should not be forced into the fingers but placed gently." Oxford Health NHS advice for care staff: "Fit the palm protector by gently prising open the fingers and thumb ... slide the ... pad under the fingers." Two hands are needed by the hand itself: its curled fingers spring shut the moment they are let go and the fist leaves no room for the cone, so one hand holds the fingers open while the other lays the cone in the palm; then the fingers are eased down onto it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) Pad, fixed: firm foam with a light blue wipe-clean cover, 46 x 39 x 2 cm, x 10 to 56, y -25 to 14. (2) Training hand, loose, 0.58 kg (forearm and palm one hollow shell, 0.50 kg): an adult woman's right forearm and hand at true size (ANSUR II women's means: hand 181 mm long, 78 mm across, palm 109 mm), soft vinyl, skin colour, lying palm up on the pad, fingers pointing toward the robot (-x), thumb to the robot's left; knuckle axis along y at x 24.0, z 3.5; palm x 22.6 to 33.1 (wrist crease), y 0.1 to 7.9; forearm cut 20 cm above the wrist, to x 53.1. The fingers are curled into a fist by springs: the four knuckles turn together (0.08 N m/rad, resting at 90 deg; each finger with 8 deg open and 6 deg closed of sprung play, 0.15 N m/rad), each middle joint on its own spring (0.02 N m/rad; resting at 106, 102, 98 and 88 deg, index to little), end joints fixed at 30 deg; the fingertips rest 0.6 to 1.0 cm above the palm; the thumb lies along the index finger on a spring about the vertical (0.03 N m/rad). Build files: fabrication/ (STL, drawing, parts). (3) Palm cone, loose: a firm terry-covered cone, 13 cm long, 2.5 cm across at its narrow end and 4.2 cm at its wide end, 0.07 kg, a white elastic band along it, lying on its side on the pad, axis along y, wide end toward -y, centre x 26.0, y -15.5. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every control step: each finger's knuckle and middle-joint angles, the thumb's, where the hand lies, where the cone lies in the hand, each fingertip's distance from the cone, and each gripper finger's collision-hull points. 0 for the rest of the run once a rule is broken: a knuckle opening faster than 90 deg/s (a finger jerked open); any finger joint closing faster than 150 deg/s (let snap shut); a knuckle opened past straight, or a middle joint straightened to under 30 deg of bend; the thumb pushed out over 35 deg; a finger touching the cone pushed open over 10 deg at the knuckle (the cone forced into the fingers); the hand lifted over 1 cm or moved over 2 cm along the pad. Otherwise the best stage reached: 0.25 all four knuckles bent 45 deg or less at once (fingers held open); 0.5 the cone seated in the palm: its axis within 25 deg of the knuckle line, narrow end at the thumb side (3 cm inside to 2.5 cm beyond the index finger's outer edge), its middle at most 4 cm behind the knuckle line, its lowest point over the palm within 1 cm of the palm's surface; 0.75 seated with all four fingertips on it (within 2.5 mm); 1.0 (success, held 1 s): that, every gripper finger point 3 cm or more from hand and cone, cone and fingers still (under 1 mm and 0.5 deg over 1 s). Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: a side video with a protractor card behind the knuckles gives the angles and speeds (over 3 deg of opening or 5 deg of closing between frames 1/30 s apart breaks a rule); a photo from above with a ruler along the knuckles gives where the cone lies and which fingertips touch it; tape marks on the pad show the hand's drift.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the hand palm up with its knuckles and forearm end on their taped marks on the pad and let the fingers close by themselves; lay the cone on its side on its mark, wide end toward the robot's right. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The hand is a moulded shell (smooth meshes from adult women's means, not a scan) with rounded finger segments; it collides as convex hulls, so the hollow of the palm is filled. The four knuckles share one sprung joint with a little sprung play per finger; end joints are fixed; no tendons, skin give or changing tone. The cone is rigid (a firm cone under a thin terry cover); its strap is not modelled. Skin, pad and cone do not deform.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper went down to the cone again and again, nudging it on the pad, but never took hold of it; the left arm stayed back and the fingers were never opened); demo: 1.0
